description: Arsenic trioxide is recommended, within its marketing authorisation, as an option for inducing remission and consolidation in acute promyelocytic leukaemia (characterised by the presence of the t(15;17) translocation or the PML/RAR-alpha gene) in adults with: untreated, low-to-intermediate risk disease (white blood cell count of 10x10^3 per microlitre or less), when given with all-trans-retinoic acid (ATRA); or relapsed or refractory disease, after a retinoid and chemotherapy.

extensions.name: statement description
extensions.value: The U.K. National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has recommended arsenic trioxide, within its marketing authorisation, as an option for inducing remission and consolidation in acute promyelocytic leukaemia in adults, either untreated with low-to-intermediate risk disease (given with all-trans-retinoic acid) or relapsed or refractory disease after a retinoid and chemotherapy. Arsenic trioxide is recommended within its marketing authorisation and subject to the commercial arrangement available to the NHS.
